summary: Color in text prompt using commands
description:
This is a bug where you can insert colors into the user's text prompt with command blocks (namely using /tellraw).
Example:

```
/tellraw @a {"text":"Click","color":"blue","clickEvent":{"action":"suggest_command","value":"\u00a7bChat was replaced with colored text"}}
```
Note that, when the message is sent, you will be kicked for "illegal characters in chat" or similar on servers, and the singleplayer game will freeze (which is MC-79818)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Place a command block and open its command interface.
4. Enter `/tellraw @a {"text":"Click","color":"blue","clickEvent":{"action":"suggest_command","value":"\u00a7bChat was replaced with colored text"}}` into the command block.
5. Activate the command block to send the message.
6. Click the displayed “Click” text to insert the suggested command into the chat prompt.
7. Send the inserted text in chat.
8. Observe that the singleplayer game freezes; on a server, observe that the player is kicked for “illegal characters in chat” or similar.
Observed Behavior:
### Actual behavior

When the command is executed, the `tellraw` message displays **“Click”** in blue and provides a clickable `suggest_command` event. Clicking the message inserts the event’s value into the player’s chat input:

```text
§bChat was replaced with colored text
```

The inserted section-sign formatting code (`§b`) is not sanitized before the text is submitted. Sending this text on a multiplayer server causes the player to be disconnected with an error such as **“Illegal characters in chat”**. In singleplayer, submitting the text causes the game to freeze, as tracked by **MC-79818**.
Expected Behavior: When a `/tellraw` message suggests text containing color formatting, the suggested text should be handled safely in the chat prompt without causing an “illegal characters in chat” kick or freezing the game. The player should remain connected and able to edit, send, or cancel the suggested command normally, with the message’s intended formatting preserved where supported.
